result.title: Anchor: Augmented Cross-Layer Recurrent State for Long-Context Retrieval in Test-Time Training
result.comment: 10 Pages main paper with reference and appendix
result.summary: Parameter-efficient linearization turns a pretrained autoregressive Transformer into an efficient model by hybridizing sliding-window attention (SWA) with a constant-size recurrent memory. But does every layer's recurrent state contribute to long-context retrieval? Investigating an SWA and Test-Time Training (TTT) hybrid, we find that retrieval is sparse across depth, concentrated in a few anchor layers, and that the remaining states hold similar information expressed through layer-specific transformations. We exploit both observations in Anchor: TTT memory placed only at the anchor layers, and a cross-layer recurrent state written once and read by many layers, each through its own learned read map that realizes a layer-specific stretch and rotation, along with demonstrated generalization to other hybrid attentions. On Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B, Anchor delivers 2.3-3.1x higher recall and 6.7-8.9 points higher MMLU accuracy than LoLCATs with a 10x smaller recurrent state, retains 91-95% of the teacher's MMLU accuracy, and cuts end-to-end latency by up to 4.3x relative to softmax attention.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究线性化 Transformer 的跨层循环状态如何服务长上下文检索，发现检索集中于少数 anchor 层，并提出只在 anchor 层放置 TTT memory、让多层通过各自 read map 读写共享状态。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非视觉工作，但其对「检索能力沿深度稀疏分布」的分析和跨层共享、层适应读取机制，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态应置于哪些层、如何跨层复用并减少视觉证据损失。
